candidate.analysis: The program reads /input/public_csv, filters to ethics-focused debates when identifiable from philosophical_topic or topic_of_debate, and reports sample size, target summaries by moderator stance and critical-event status, Pearson correlations for numeric predictors, and simple least-squares coefficients including moderator/event indicators. It prints concise observations only and does not claim causal or scientific validity.
candidate.answer: Among 259 ethics-focused debates, percentage increase in utilitarian advocacy averaged 17.330%. Argument intensity could not be assessed due to unavailable variation. Audience interest showed essentially no relationship (r=-0.006), while average debate duration (r=0.074) and number of sessions (r=0.053) showed very weak positive relationships. Moderator stance was strongly associated: utilitarian moderators averaged 65.189%, versus 0.054% for deontological and 0.570% for virtue-ethics moderators. Debates with critical events averaged 29.441%, compared with 6.143% without events; 34 cases had missing event status and averaged 18.046%. These are observational associations, not causal conclusions.
